nlm_primary_record.title: Cadherin-26 contributes to intraepithelial eosinophil and neutrophil infiltration in chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps.
nlm_primary_record.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) features marked infiltration of diverse inflammatory cells. Cadherin-26 (CDH26) is an adhesion molecule associated with eosinophilic inflammation, but its role in CRSwNP remains undefined.
OBJECTIVE: We investigated the expression, mechanism, and function of CDH26 in CRSwNP.
METHODS: Bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing and immunohistochemistry of human nasal tissues profiled CDH26 expression and localization as well as its association with immune cells and inflammatory pathways in CRSwNP. Nasal epithelial cells were stimulated with cytokines to examine CDH26 expression and were transfected to evaluate CDH26's impact on JAK-STAT signaling. Adhesion and survival assays were conducted with isolated eosinophils and neutrophils. CDH26-/- mice were used to establish a CRSwNP model to determine CDH26's role in disease development.
RESULTS: CDH26 was elevated in eosinophilic CRSwNP compared to control and noneosinophilic CRSwNP and correlated with intraepithelial infiltration of both eosinophils and neutrophils. Single-cell analysis showed its epithelial localization and coexpression with IL13RA1/STAT6 in basal cells. CDH26 was induced by IL-4/IL-13 via JAK-STAT signaling and in turn enhanced STAT6 phosphorylation. CDH26 mediated epithelial adhesion of eosinophils and neutrophils via integrin α4 (aka ITGA4) and enhanced their survival in vitro. CDH26-/- mice showed attenuated nasal polyp-like lesion formation and reduction in the infiltration of eosinophils, neutrophils, mast cells, and T-cell subsets.
CONCLUSION: CDH26 is a type 2-inducible epithelial molecule that functions as an inflammatory mediator in CRSwNP by modulating JAK-STAT signaling and promoting eosinophil and neutrophil retention, thereby linking epithelial dysfunction to sustained inflammation and may represent a potential therapeutic target.

nlm_primary_record.title: IL-9R/Arg1 pathway promotes polyamine metabolism in human airway macrophages.
nlm_primary_record.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lung macrophages are central regulators of inflammatory responses in the airways and lung parenchyma. Macrophages function as conduits for cytokine function in the inflammatory milieu. We previously demonstrated that IL-9-responsive macrophages are essential for allergic lung inflammation in an arginase 1 (Arg1) pathway.
OBJECTIVE: We defined the IL-9/Arg1/polyamine pathway in human macrophages from model systems and asthmatic patient samples.
METHODS: Using humanized NSG-Quad mice treated with intranasal IL-9 and patient bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) samples, we evaluated macrophage phenotypes via flow cytometry, bulk RNA sequencing, and metabolic assays.
RESULTS: Two distinct human lung macrophage populations were defined by the expression of CD43. IL-9 promoted the expansion of IL-9R+/Arg1+CD43- macrophages in humanized mice. In parallel, greater proportions of IL-9R+/Arg1+CD43- macrophages were observed in asthmatic patient BAL samples compared to healthy control patients. Higher concentrations of polyamines, downstream metabolites of Arg1 function, were detected in BAL of IL-9-treated humanized mice. There were increased concentrations of polyamines in asthmatic patient BAL compared to control samples, and concentrations were positively correlated to BAL IL-9 concentration and increases of IL-9R+ and Arg1+CD43- macrophages.
CONCLUSIONS: IL-9-responsive CD206+CD43- macrophages alter the metabolites present in the lung milieu. These data provide evidence for an IL-9R/Arg1/polyamine lung macrophage axis that is active in asthma patients.

nlm_primary_record.title: Barzolvolimab blocks stem cell factor-enhanced IgE activation without inducing apoptosis in KITD816V mast cells.
nlm_primary_record.abstract:
BACKGROUND: KITD816V drives constitutive mast cell (MC) signaling and is central to the pathogenesis of clonal MC activation disorders, including systemic mastocytosis. These conditions may present with severe anaphylaxis despite low KITD816V mutation burden. Because neoplastic MCs may coexpress mutant and wild-type (WT) KIT, the functional relevance of ligand-dependent signaling and activation remains incompletely understood. Barzolvolimab has demonstrated efficacy in WT MC-driven diseases, but its effects on KIT-mutated MCs remain unclear.
OBJECTIVE: We assessed the effects of barzolvolimab on KITD816V-mutated MCs.
METHODS: We established and characterized primary-like human MC models, including isogenic human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived WT and heterozygous KITD816V MCs, peripheral CD34+ stem cell-derived MCs, and HMC-1.2 cell line. Barzolvolimab effects on apoptosis, KIT signaling, and IgE-mediated activation were investigated by flow cytometry, Western blot analysis, and functional degranulation assays.
RESULTS: Barzolvolimab induced dose-dependent apoptosis and inhibited stem cell factor-induced KIT signaling in WT MCs, but it had no effect on mutant MC viability or signaling. Notably, barzolvolimab effectively suppressed stem cell factor-enhanced IgE-mediated MC activation across all primary-like models, including KITD816V MCs, as evidenced by reduced β-hexosaminidase release and CD63 expression. This inhibitory effect occurred at low nanomolar concentrations and was independent of cytotoxicity.
CONCLUSIONS: A functional dissociation between KIT-dependent survival and activation pathways occurs in mutated MCs. Barzolvolimab does not reduce the viability of KIT-mutated MCs, but it effectively suppresses stem cell factor-dependent amplification of IgE-mediated activation, thus supporting its potential as a therapeutic option for symptomatic patients harboring KIT mutations, particularly for the control of mediator-related symptoms.

source_evidence.title: Staphylococcus aureus serine protease-like protein B is a potent allergen in a murine asthma model

nlm_primary_record.title: Staphylococcus aureus serine protease-like protein B is a potent allergen in a murine asthma model.
nlm_primary_record.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Asthma is associated with Staphylococcus aureus colonization. Two hypotheses are proposed to explain this phenomenon: (1) the allergic environment in asthma favors S aureus colonization, and (2) S aureus colonization creates a proallergic environment. Because several S aureus virulence factors, such as the serine protease-like protein (Spl) B, elicit a type 2-biased immune response, we asked whether the pathogen itself can cause asthma.
OBJECTIVE: We tested the ability of recombinant SplB of S aureus to sensitize mice and induce allergic airway inflammation (AAI).
METHODS: Mice were treated with repeated intratracheal inoculations of either catalytically active SplB or an inactive mutant. AAI was assessed by evaluating airway hypersensitivity, immune cell infiltration, cytokines, mucus production, fibrosis, and specific serum IgE. We compared the outcome between wild-type and gene-deficient C57BL/6J mice, including recombination-activating gene knockout mice (Rag2-/-), IL-33 knockout mice (Il33-/-), and protease-activated receptor 2 knockout mice (F2rl1-/-).
RESULTS: Intratracheal exposure to SplB sensitized the mice and caused eosinophilic airway inflammation and hyperresponsiveness. The development of asthma required both the proteolytic activity of SplB and a functional adaptive immune system. The soluble protease sensor IL-33 was necessary for eosinophil tissue invasion, whereas the membrane-bound protease sensor PAR2 was not.
CONCLUSION: The serine protease SplB of S aureus is a potent allergen. On the basis of this finding, we propose a third mechanism to explain the relationship between S aureus colonization and asthma: S aureus can release allergens, such as SplB, that sensitize individuals and lead to the development of asthma.

nlm_primary_record.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate monitoring of B-cell reconstitution is dependent on age-specific pediatric reference ranges. However, pediatric CD19+ B-cell reference values currently lack harmonization and are inconsistently defined.
OBJECTIVE: We sought to systematically evaluate published pediatric reference values for CD19+ B cells in healthy children and adolescents (age range, 0-18 years).
METHODS: This review and meta-analysis was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses) 2020 guidelines. A comprehensive literature search was performed for studies reporting CD19+ B cells in healthy children from 2000 to 2025 (final search in March 2025). Records were independently screened and assessed for quality by 3 investigators. Data for lower limit of normal (lower limit of 95% reference interval) were analyzed and compared for different age groups.
RESULTS: After screening, 29 publications met the inclusion criteria, representing a total cohort of 10,399 individuals. Our analysis showed that the lower limit of normal of CD19+ B-cell values differed according to the age of the child. We identified 5 distinct age groups and corresponding values of lower limit of normal. In children younger than 6 years, B-cell values were consistently different from values that have been reported for adults.
CONCLUSION: This systematic synthesis summarizes consolidated age-stratified lower limits of normal values for CD19+ B cells in children and adolescents. Proposed CD19+ B-cell values can be used for standardized clinical monitoring of B-cell recovery to normal values after CD19-depleting therapy.

nlm_primary_record.title: ABACHAI phase 2 clinical trial: Safety and efficacy of subcutaneous abatacept in patients with CTLA-4 insufficiency or LRBA deficiency.
nlm_primary_record.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heterozygous germline mutations in CTLA4 (CTLA-4 insufficiency) and biallelic mutations in LRBA (lipopolysaccharide-responsive beige-like anchor protein [LRBA] deficiency) cause immune dysregulation with autoimmunity, lymphoproliferation, and immunodeficiency. For treatment, abatacept has been used successfully and is increasingly being used off-label; however, prospective clinical trial data are missing.
OBJECTIVE: We evaluated the safety and efficacy of abatacept in patients with CTLA-4 insufficiency or LRBA deficiency.
METHODS: ABACHAI was a prospective, open-label, single-arm phase 2a trial. Adult patients with genetically confirmed CTLA-4 insufficiency or LRBA deficiency and at least one clinically significant organ manifestation received 125 mg abatacept subcutaneously once a week for 12 months. The primary end point was safety, defined as the number of episodes of failed infection control. Secondary end points included additional safety parameters, efficacy outcomes, and patient-reported quality of life.
RESULTS: Twenty patients were enrolled (18 with CTLA-4 insufficiency and 2 with LRBA deficiency). Three patients had 5 severe infections during treatment (incidence rate, 0.27 per patient-year), comparable to the year before enrollment. No Epstein-Barr virus or cytomegalovirus reactivations occurred. Abatacept reduced lymphoproliferation and immune activation and improved patient-reported quality of life and gastrointestinal symptom quality. Cytopenias and renal involvement were not sufficiently controlled. Four patients (20%) discontinued therapy, 3 because of unrelated serious adverse events and 1 because of noncompliance.
CONCLUSION: ABACHAI was the first prospective interventional trial examining abatacept treatment in CTLA-4 insufficiency and LRBA deficiency. Abatacept demonstrated a favorable safety profile and organ-specific efficacy, with strongest responses in lymphoproliferation and immune activation. Patients with refractory cytopenias or progressive organ involvement may require additional or alternative therapeutic strategies.

nlm_primary_record.title: Nasal epithelial transcriptome-wide isoform-level expression and asthma endotypes in youth.
nlm_primary_record.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Previous transcriptome-wide association studies of asthma lacked analyses of isoform expression.
OBJECTIVE: We sought to identify isoforms associated with asthma endotypes in children and adolescents.
METHODS: Meta-analysis of association between isoform- and gene-level nasal epithelial expression and TH2-high or TH17-high asthma (with TH2-low/TH17-low asthma as the reference group) in 459 youths with asthma aged 8-20 years in 3 studies: Epigenetic Variation and Childhood Asthma in Puerto Ricans (EVA-PR), Stress and Treatment Response in Puerto Rican and African American Children With Asthma (STAR), and Vitamin D Kids Asthma (VDKA). Genes or isoforms with the same direction of association with an endotype in all cohorts and a meta-analysis false discovery rate-adjusted P < .01 were considered to have significantly differential expression.
RESULTS: In total, 6,607 isoforms encoded by 5,168 genes were associated with TH2-high asthma; 1,019 (19.7%) of these 5,168 genes were only identified in the isoform analysis, including CTNND1, CREM, TAOK2, and AIM1. A total of 4,430 isoforms encoded by 3,643 genes were associated with TH17-high asthma; 371 (10.2%) of these genes were only identified in the isoform analysis, including PSAP, FAM65B, and CFLAR. While top findings in the gene- and isoform-level analyses often overlapped, the isoforms of many genes showed differential isoform usage. In TH2-high asthma, 499 genes (encoding 731 isoforms) altered isoform usage, including CDH26, IL1RL1, MAP2K6, and SLC39A8. In TH17-high asthma, 113 genes (encoding 160 isoforms) altered isoform usage, including SBNO2, PSMB8, and NCOA7.
CONCLUSIONS: An isoform-level analysis complemented a gene-level analysis of expression and identified novel genes for asthma endotypes.

nlm_primary_record.title: Mechanistic and clinical updates in chronic rhinosinusitis: 2023 to 2025.
nlm_primary_record.abstract: Chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) is a chronic inflammatory condition of the nose and paranasal sinuses associated with poor quality of life and high health care burden. CRS is broadly classified into 2 subtypes on the basis of whether nasal polyps are present (CRSwNP) or absent (CRSsNP). Although CRSsNP is more prevalent, the underlying mechanisms contributing to CRSwNP pathogenesis have been more extensively defined over the years. CRSwNP is characterized by type 2 inflammation as well as epithelial barrier dysfunction, and in the past 3 years, a new endotype has been defined, inflammatory cell heterogeneity has been identified, novel cell populations have been discovered, and mechanisms contributing to epithelial barrier dysfunction have been advanced. Clinically, 4 biologics targeting type 2 inflammation are now FDA-approved for CRSwNP. As these therapies become increasingly common in clinical practice, ongoing investigations have focused on comparing their efficacy and defining their role alongside more established interventions such as corticosteroids and sinus surgery. In this review, novel mechanistic findings and recent clinical developments in CRS between 2023 and 2025 have been highlighted.

nlm_primary_record.title: Standardized Human Phenotype Ontology annotation enables high-quality phenotypic data capture in a real-world common variable immunodeficiency cohort.
nlm_primary_record.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with common variable immunodeficiency (CVID) exhibit diverse clinical manifestations, indicating heterogeneity in pathogenic mechanisms. Systematic application of standardized phenotyping in large cohorts is essential to dissect this heterogeneity. The Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) provides a structured framework for capturing and comparing disease phenotypes.
OBJECTIVE: We evaluated the application of systematic HPO-based phenotyping in CVID patients enrolled for whole-genome sequencing in a large national adult primary immunodeficiency cohort.
METHODS: We developed a web-based Phenotype Capture Tool and delivered structured clinician training to standardize HPO annotation. Numerical laboratory parameters were mapped to corresponding HPO terms to enrich patient records.
RESULTS: We coded the phenotypes of 526 CVID patients across 11 centers in the United Kingdom. Clinician training increased phenotype granularity and improved phenotyping consistency between clinicians. We assigned 883 unique HPO terms across the cohort and applied logical rules to the terms to classify cases into an infection-only group and a complex phenotype group (42% vs 58%, respectively). Patients in the complex phenotype group were significantly more likely to have reduced switched memory and expanded CD21low B cells, as well as pathogenic variants in International Union of Immunological Societies-listed genes overall and pathogenic NFKB1 variants specifically. Having a pathogenic variant in a listed gene was associated with Autoimmune hemolytic anemia [HP:0001890] and having a pathogenic NFKB1 variant specifically was associated with Autoimmune neutropenia [HP:0001904].
CONCLUSION: This is the first study to systematically collect granular HPO-coded phenotypes in a large real-world CVID cohort, refining the CVID landscape and providing a comprehensive CVID HPO term set relevant for international research.

nlm_primary_record.title: Selective KIT inhibition supports mast cells as key drivers of allergic asthma pathogenesis.
nlm_primary_record.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Asthma is a chronic respiratory disease characterized by airway inflammation, airway hyperresponsiveness, and airway remodeling. Mast cell numbers are increased in asthmatic airways and contribute to bronchoconstriction and inflammation, but their role in asthma development remains elusive.
OBJECTIVE: We investigated mast cell contributions to allergic asthma by pharmacologically targeting KIT, a central regulator of mast cell survival and activation, using the selective inhibitor THB001.
METHODS: THB001 effects were assessed in human lung mast cells, isolated human bronchi, and guinea pig trachea. To probe mast cell contributions in vivo, guinea pigs were subjected to a house dust mite (HDM)-induced asthma model and treated with THB001. HDM-induced bronchoconstriction was recorded after each challenge. At the end point, airway responsiveness was evaluated, followed by bronchoalveolar lavage fluid and lung tissue collection for histologic, biochemical, and transcriptomic analyses.
RESULTS: THB001 suppressed KIT-dependent mast cell functions, inhibiting human lung mast cell degranulation and survival as well as attenuating anti-IgE-induced bronchial contraction. In guinea pig tracheal segments, THB001 reduced HDM-induced responses, coinciding with a reduction in mast cells. In vivo, THB001 remodeled HDM-induced transcriptional signatures and lipid mediator release, prevented HDM-induced bronchoconstriction and airway hyperresponsiveness, and largely attenuated HDM-induced increases in mast cells, inflammation, airway smooth muscle layer thickening, and collagen deposition, with partial reduction of mucus-producing cells.
CONCLUSIONS: Mast cell-dependent signaling is a key driver of allergic asthma pathogenesis. Pharmacologic inhibition of KIT effectively suppresses mast cell activity and prevents hallmark functional and structural features of asthma in a guinea pig model, supporting KIT inhibition as a potential therapeutic approach for allergic asthma.

nlm_primary_record.title: Epidermal HLA-DQB1 exerts negative regulation of mast cell activation through the TSLP-driven SPP1-expressing macrophage axis.
nlm_primary_record.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Keratinocytes (KCs) and MHC class II are implicated in inflammatory skin diseases. However, the precise expression profiles and causal role of KC-intrinsic MHC class II in urticaria remain largely undefined.
OBJECTIVE: We sought to investigate the causal relationship and functional mechanism of epidermal MHC class II in IgE-mediated skin inflammation.
METHODS: Mendelian randomization and immunohistochemistry were employed to evaluate the genetic and clinical relevance of MHC class II in urticaria. A KC-specific H2-Ab1 knockout mouse model (K14Cre/+H2-Ab1fl/f) was generated, and IgE-induced passive cutaneous anaphylaxis was assessed. Functional validation was performed using pharmacologic activation/inhibition. Immune responses and downstream signaling pathways were characterized using flow cytometry, single-cell RNA sequencing, chromatin immunoprecipitation assay, RNA interference, luciferase reporter gene assays, and Western blotting.
RESULTS: Mendelian randomization analysis identified a protective causal effect of skin HLA-DQB1 expression on urticaria risk. Epidermal MHC class II levels negatively correlated with disease severity and positively correlated with disease control scores in patients. Epidermal H2-Ab1 knockout exacerbated passive cutaneous anaphylaxis responses in mice. Mechanistically, deletion of HLA-DQB1/H2-Ab1 in KCs reduced repressive trimethylated histone 3 lysine 9 at the thymic stromal lymphopoietin (TSLP) promoter via downregulation of SUV39H1, leading to TSLP overexpression. TSLP promoted SPP1 expression in macrophages, polarizing a proinflammatory SPP1+ subset. SPP1 directly activated mast cells (MCs), enhancing degranulation and inflammatory mediator release. This KC-macrophage-MC axis was validated in coculture systems.
CONCLUSION: Epidermal HLA-DQB1/H2-Ab1 negatively regulates IgE-mediated skin inflammation by epigenetically suppressing TSLP expression, thereby restraining a TSLP-SPP1+ macrophage-MC activation cascade. These findings reveal a novel immunoregulatory function of KC MHC class II and highlight the HLA-DQB1-TSLP-SPP1+ macrophage axis as a potential therapeutic target in urticaria.

nlm_primary_record.title: MITF-associated metabolic signature in mast cells: A potential link to food anaphylaxis.
nlm_primary_record.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Microphthalmia-associated transcription factor (MITF) is a master regulator of mast cell (MC) differentiation and effector function; it is essential for anaphylaxis (severe allergic reactions). Although MITF has been linked to mitochondrial regulation through pyruvate dehydrogenase, whether it broadly controls mitochondrial fitness and metabolic programs that exacerbate MC activation remains unclear.
OBJECTIVE: Our aim was to determine how MITF regulates MC mitochondrial function and metabolic fitness beyond pyruvate dehydrogenase control, as well as to define its contribution to heightened MC activation and food anaphylaxis.
METHODS: MITF was silenced, pharmacologically inhibited, or overexpressed in human MCs, followed by IgE- and MRGPRX2-dependent activation. Transcriptomic profiling and mitochondrial functional analyses were then performed. In parallel, MCs from patients with food anaphylaxis and from healthy controls were analyzed to assess clinical relevance.
RESULTS: Transcriptomic analysis of MITF-silenced MCs revealed a distinct metabolic signature characterized by downregulation of mitochondrial pathways and metabolic cellular compartments. MITF knockdown reduced mitochondrial fission, membrane potential, mitochondrial respiration, and mitochondrial marker expression of TOM20 and COX-IV, supporting a role for MITF in mitochondrial activity and metabolic regulation. Furthermore, compared with MCs from sensitized and healthy individuals, MCs from patients with food anaphylaxis exhibited increased MITF expression, elevated levels of mitochondrial markers, enhanced mitochondrial respiration, and a glycolytic shift after allergen activation,. Notably, pharmacologic inhibition of MITF reduced mitochondrial membrane potential in patient-derived MCs.
CONCLUSIONS: MITF is a central regulator of MC mitochondrial function; it is associated with enhanced metabolic activity in anaphylaxis, highlighting MITF-driven pathways as potential therapeutic targets in MC-mediated allergic disease.

nlm_primary_record.title: Autosomal-recessive HOXA3 deficiency causes congenital athymia and laryngeal malformation.
nlm_primary_record.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Approximately 10% of patients with severe combined immunodeficiency phenotype lack a known genetic cause. In particular, the molecular basis of thymic defects is poorly understood. Homeobox (HOX) genes encode conserved transcription factors that control spatial body development. The function of human HOXA3 is undefined.
OBJECTIVE: We characterized the first human with HOXA3 deficiency and investigated the role of HOXA3 in immune system development.
METHODS: We performed clinical and immunologic phenotyping as well as genetic sequencing. A homozygous nonsense variant in HOXA3 was identified and functionally validated via reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction, Western blot analysis, assessment of transcriptional activity, and intracellular localization of HOXA3. We report clinical management and course.
RESULTS: The homozygous HOXA3 nonsense variant generates a truncated protein with cytoplasmic retention and reduced transcriptional activity. The clinical phenotype includes craniofacial and cervical anomalies, severe laryngopharyngeal malformation with epiglottic hypoplasia causing dysphagia and aspiration, central breathing disorder, and thymus aplasia. T-cell maturation in artificial thymic organoids and recovery after thymus transplantation establish the T-cell defect as nonhematopoietic.
CONCLUSION: Human HOXA3 has nonredundant roles for the development of larynx and thymus. HOXA3 deficiency is a novel, life-threatening multisystem disorder. It is the first human homeobox-gene disease causing congenital athymia. These findings expand the diagnostic gene panel for patients with a severe combined immunodeficiency phenotype and indicate epiglottic hypoplasia as a new specific comorbidity of congenital athymia.

nlm_primary_record.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The MESILICO (Efficacy of Mepolizumab in patients with latE-onset Severe eosInophiLic asthma and fIxed obstruCtiOn) study has provided evidence on the effect of mepolizumab, an anti-IL-5 biologic, on airway remodeling in patients with severe asthma at 12 months posttreatment.
OBJECTIVE: We sought to investigate the longer-term effect of mepolizumab on airway structural remodeling.
METHODS: Forty-seven patients were recruited, who initiated mepolizumab (100 mg mepolizumab subcutaneously), of whom 41 were enrolled in the bronchoscopy substudy. At 3 years, the participants underwent further bronchoscopic airway sampling, and remodeling indices were measured along with submucosal eosinophils, tissue immunoexpression of mucin 5AC, E-cadherin, and number of FOXP3+ cells.
RESULTS: Thirty-five of the initial 47 patients in the cohort completed 3 years of treatment, associated with significant improvements in lung function and biomarkers and a decrease in exacerbation events (P < .05). Twenty-five of the 41 patients enrolled in the substudy were submitted to bronchoscopy after 3 years of treatment. There was a significant sustained reduction from baseline in subbasement membrane thickness, airway smooth muscle area, airway smooth muscle layer thickness, and epithelial damage, as well as a decrease in the number of tissue eosinophils (all P < .001). Additional improvements were seen at 3 years for mucin 5AC and E-cadherin histoscores and FOXP3+ regulatory-like cells.
CONCLUSIONS: This is the first study supporting the possibility that sustained IL-5 blockade may contribute to long-term structural airway improvement and may be consistent with disease modification in severe eosinophilic asthma.

nlm_primary_record.title: miRNA profiling identifies biomarkers and regulatory networks involving TGF-β/T-cell pathways in food protein-induced enterocolitis syndrome.
nlm_primary_record.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute food protein-induced enterocolitis syndrome (FPIES) is a potentially life-threatening, non-IgE-mediated food allergy that primarily affects young children. Currently, diagnosis relies on clinical presentation and oral food challenges, which carry inherent risks. Consequently, FPIES is often misdiagnosed, leading to unnecessary interventions and delayed management. Despite its clinical relevance, the molecular mechanisms underlying FPIES remain poorly understood.
OBJECTIVE: We investigated the role of microRNAs (miRNAs) in FPIES and assessed their diagnostic potential.
METHODS: We analyzed miRNA expression profiles in peripheral blood from 29 children with oral food challenge-confirmed moderate to severe FPIES reactions, collected on the challenge day at baseline (TP1), reaction onset (TP2), and 4 hours after reaction onset (TP3). Using a hybrid ensemble feature selection approach, we compared these profiles to those of 26 children with acute gastroenteritis and sepsis to identify FPIES-specific miRNA signatures.
RESULTS: Longitudinal analysis revealed an early heterogeneous miRNA response that evolved into a more consistent profile in TP3, suggesting a dynamic and evolving regulatory response. Eleven miRNAs emerged as key regulators, highlighting pathways partially shared with other allergic and inflammatory conditions. In silico pathway analysis identified TGF-β signaling and T-cell differentiation as candidate pathways potentially involved in FPIES. Importantly, we discovered and validated 26 miRNAs signatures that accurately distinguish FPIES from sepsis and acute gastroenteritis, including a minimal 2-miRNA diagnostic signature (area under the curve = 0.98). miRNA-29a correlated with severe FPIES reactions, suggesting involvement in severity mechanisms.
CONCLUSION: Our study reveals novel miRNA-mediated mechanisms in FPIES and identifies candidate biomarkers with diagnostic utility, paving the way for new molecular tools and therapeutic strategies.

nlm_primary_record.title: Leniolisib and rapamycin in activated PI3Kδ syndrome: Retrospective European Society for Immunodeficiencies registry-based analysis.
nlm_primary_record.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Activated PI3Kδ syndrome (APDS) is a rare inborn error of immunity characterized by variable immune dysregulation, recurrent infections, and increased risk of malignancy. Clinical management is challenging. Rapamycin has been widely used off-label to control immune dysregulation, while the selective PI3Kδ (phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase delta) inhibitor leniolisib has recently become available as a disease-specific targeted therapy. Real-world data on these treatment approaches remain limited.
OBJECTIVE: We assessed real-world treatment indications, clinical course, immunologic changes, and tolerability in patients with APDS treated with rapamycin and leniolisib.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective analysis of the European Society for Immunodeficiencies APDS registry including 95 APDS patients, 81 treated with rapamycin and/or 28 with leniolisib through a Managed Access Program. Clinical manifestations, immunologic parameters, and treatment-associated complications were assessed.
RESULTS: Lymphoproliferation was the predominant indication (81% and 52%, respectively) for treatment initiation. Overall responses (complete or partial) were observed in 67% of rapamycin- and 64% of leniolisib-treated patients. Across other disease manifestations, responses were documented in 35% and 50% of patients. Leniolisib was initiated for recurrent infections in 3 patients, whereas recurrent infections were not a primary indication for rapamycin. Treatment interruption due to adverse events occurred only in the rapamycin group. Lymphoma cases were observed during follow-up.

nlm_primary_record.title: Functional evaluation of chimeric antigen receptor T-cell anti-CD123 from immune-mediated inflammatory disease patients for novel plasmacytoid dendritic cell-targeted immunotherapy.
nlm_primary_record.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chimeric antigen receptor T (CAR-T) cell therapy is a promising approach for immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMIDs). Plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDCs), which infiltrate tissues and secrete type I interferons, play a central early role in IMIDs and represent an attractive therapeutic target.
OBJECTIVE: Given the high CD123 expression on pDCs, we assessed the potential of CD123 CAR-T cells to eliminate pDCs across multiple IMIDs.
METHODS: In the CARDA2I study, patients with psoriasis, hidradenitis suppurativa, systemic lupus erythematosus, or systemic sclerosis were enrolled regardless of disease severity or treatment. After peripheral blood mononuclear cells were collected from patients and healthy donors (HDs), extended phenotype T cells were characterized at day 0 (D0) and after 10 days of expansion (D10). CAR-T cell functionality was assessed by coculture with autologous peripheral blood mononuclear cells and in BRGSF-HIS mice treated with human Flt3 ligand and imiquimod-induced psoriasis.
RESULTS: Patient T cells showed phenotypic alterations at D0, which normalized by D10 after expansion. Patient-derived CD123 CAR-T cells efficiently eliminated pDCs in vitro and in vivo and migrated to inflamed skin. In mice, CAR-T cell treatment reduced pDC skin infiltration, restored epidermal architecture, and decreased psoriasiform inflammation.
CONCLUSION: Autologous T cells from IMID patients can generate functional CD123 CAR-T cells comparable to healthy donors. These cells effectively deplete pDCs and improve psoriasis-like skin pathology, supporting their potential as a novel cell-based therapy in pDC-driven IMIDs.

nlm_primary_record.title: Prostaglandin E2 protects against MRGPRX2/Mrgprb2-mediated and aspirin-aggravated anaphylaxis via modulation of mast cell activation.
nlm_primary_record.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, can be triggered via the Mas-related G protein-coupled receptor (MRGPR) X2 pathway and its murine ortholog, Mrgprb2. Aspirin (ASA) is known to exacerbate anaphylaxis as a result of the reduction of the homeostatic lipid mediator prostaglandin E2 (PGE2).
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to investigate the regulatory role of PGE2 in MRGPRX2/Mrgprb2-mediated anaphylaxis and to determine how ASA may aggravate anaphylactic severity.
METHODS: A murine model of systemic Mrgprb2-mediated anaphylaxis was used. Mice were treated with ASA, an inhibitor of the PGE2-degrading enzyme, and/or selective agonists targeting individual prostanoid E (EP) receptors. Mast cells were isolated from murine peritoneum and human skin, then exposed to PGE2 and EP receptor agonists or antagonists, and subjected to RNA interference experiments. Epidemiologic analyses were performed using data from the anaphylaxis registry.
RESULTS: Murine data provide evidence that endogenous PGE2 regulates ASA-potentiated, Mrgprb2-mediated anaphylaxis through EP3 and EP4 receptor signaling. Accordingly, exogenous PGE2 markedly attenuated MRGPRX2/b2-driven mast cell activation in vitro, predominantly via EP2 and EP3 receptors. These findings are supported by data from anaphylaxis registry indicating that the severity of anaphylaxis induced by drugs acting via MRGPRX2 is increased when nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs are concomitantly taken.
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings demonstrate the protective role of PGE2 through mitigating MRGPRX2/b2-mediated anaphylaxis via a direct reduction of mast cell activation. Further studies are needed to clarify whether EP receptors may serve as therapeutic targets for preventing or modifying anaphylactic responses.

nlm_primary_record.title: Restoring epithelial health in epithelial-driven disease through an early treat-to-target approach: Improving patient care toward clinical remission.
nlm_primary_record.abstract: The structure and function of the airway epithelium are central in protecting against harmful environmental insults and conserving respiratory health; however, epithelial dysfunction can contribute to airway disease. Epithelial health represents a state of equilibrium where the airway epithelial barrier, immune activity, and mucociliary dynamics work in concert to maintain tissue integrity and prevent inflammation. An invited Epithelial Science Expert Group met in London in March 2025 to discuss the current understanding of epithelial health in the airways and ways that epithelial health may be restored in upper and lower inflammatory airway disease. This review summarizes the key concepts raised during the meeting. The group discussed the benefits and drawbacks of currently available biomarkers of respiratory epithelial disruption, including mucus plugs, ventilation defects, mucin glycoproteins, cilia beat frequency, tight junction proteins, and inflammatory biomarkers. These discussions highlighted a need for biomarkers with the ability to directly assess epithelial function to improve the understanding of epithelial-driven airway disease. Approaches to restore epithelial health were also reviewed, focusing on normalization of mucin production, restoration of epithelial tight junctions, improvement of the epithelial microbiome, and stem cell therapy, all of which show clinical promise. Attendees highlighted the need for a united airways approach to respiratory disease management, involving multidisciplinary, cross-specialty care. Finally, the trajectory of respiratory epithelial injury and repair over time was explored, focusing on the role of a treat-to-target approach as well as early intervention to restore epithelial health and obtain clinical remission in patients with epithelial-driven inflammatory airway disease.

nlm_primary_record.title: Hyperactive STAT1 promotes Tfh1-cell differentiation to trigger autoimmunity.
nlm_primary_record.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heterozygous gain-of-function (GOF) mutations in signal transducer and activator of transcription 1 (STAT1) cause an inborn error of immunity characterized by immune dysregulation, recurrent infections, and various autoimmune manifestations. However, the precise pathogenic mechanism by which STAT1 GOF contributes to autoimmunity remains elusive.
OBJECTIVE: We sought to determine whether and how STAT1 GOF affects Tfh-cell differentiation and autoimmune pathogenesis.
METHODS: Using Stat1-GOF (T385M) mice, we analyzed the effects of STAT1 GOF on the Tfh differentiation and germinal center responses on various immune challenging. CUT&Tag and transcriptomic analyses were integrated to dissect how STAT1 GOF contributes to autoimmunity. Furthermore, Janus kinase inhibition and IFN-γ blockade were evaluated in vivo.
RESULTS: Patients with STAT1 GOF showed a bias in cTfh cells toward a CXCR3+ Tfh1-like phenotype. In Stat1-GOF mice, excessive STAT1 activation promoted Tfh differentiation, enhanced germinal center formation, and disturbed T-cell-dependent humoral responses, with immunoglobulin class switching skewed toward IgG2. STAT1 GOF directly targeted Tfh- and TH1-associated genes and drove the development of IFN-γ-producing Tfh1 cells, which was accompanied by autoantibody production and autoimmune manifestations. IFN-γ neutralization reduced autoimmune cellular responses and autoantibody levels in mutant mice.
CONCLUSIONS: STAT1 GOF promotes aberrant Tfh1 differentiation to drive autoimmunity and dysregulated humoral responses. These findings imply that proper regulation of STAT1 activity within a reasonable magnitude is crucial for ensuring optimal host-protective humoral immunity, and that IFN-γ neutralization may be a promising treatment option for patients with STAT1 GOF and other related autoimmune diseases.

nlm_primary_record.title: Scientific advances from sharing Urban Environment and Childhood Asthma study data in collaborative analyses.
nlm_primary_record.abstract: The National Institutes of Health-sponsored Urban Environment and Childhood Asthma (URECA) study of families in low-income, urban neighborhoods has provided important insights in this population but has a limited capacity to investigate risk factors across broader geographic and sociodemographic settings. To overcome this shortcoming, URECA investigators have shared data with multiple National Institutes of Health-sponsored birth cohorts and investigators, including the Environmental Influences on Child Health Outcomes program and the Children's Allergy and Asthma Data Repository. We collaboratively developed methods, including a novel array to measure DNA methylation at CpG sites implicated in asthma, and geospatial estimates of exposure to air pollution, social conditions, and neighborhood characteristics based on residential address. Applying these tools to pooled datasets demonstrated associations between increased asthma incidence and birth in low-income, historically redlined census tracts, residence in low-food-access census tracts, identifying as African American or Caribbean-Hispanic American, and higher air pollution. Distinct asthma phenotypes based on longitudinal patterns of clinical features were associated with specific genetic polymorphisms. Studies of nasal cells identified patterns of gene expression and nasal epithelial DNA methylation signatures associated with specific asthma and allergy phenotypes. These collaborative projects have advanced our understanding of childhood asthma and established an investigative culture of data sharing, trust, and cooperation.

nlm_primary_record.title: SERPINE1 promoter variants and differential airway responses to virus and biological therapy.
nlm_primary_record.abstract:
BACKGROUND: A common functional promoter polymorphism (4G4G/4G5G) in the SERPINE1 gene, which encodes the plasminogen activator inhibitor 1 (PAI-1) protein, is associated with more frequent asthma exacerbations.
OBJECTIVE: We examined genotype-specific airway transcriptomic responses during viral illness and how genotype modulates these responses in asthma exacerbations with and without mepolizumab treatment.
METHODS: Nasal lavage samples from a subset of children aged 6-17 years with exacerbation-prone asthma from the type 2-enriched urban asthma MUPPITS-1 and MUPPITS-2 cohorts were used for RNA sequencing and genetic studies. Expression quantitative trait locus (eQTL) analysis and weighted gene coexpression network analysis were performed to determine PAI-1 genotype modulation of gene expression during viral illness and genotype associations with mean expression levels of coexpressed networks of genes (modules). Linear regression analysis was performed to evaluate interactions between mepolizumab and the PAI-1 promoter variants.
RESULTS: Risk genotypes were associated with lower SERPINE1 expression at baseline but higher levels over the course of viral illness (P < .02). In those with the risk allele at times of viral illness, there was increased expression of 4 coexpressed networks of genes including immune/Toll-like receptor signaling, and decreased expression of one network (ribosome). Subjects with the risk allele receiving mepolizumab with nonexacerbation viral illness had higher expression of eosinophil and mucus hypersecretion gene networks. In subjects with the risk allele receiving mepolizumab who experienced exacerbation, eosinophilic signaling networks were decreased, but gene networks involved in TGF-β/SMAD3 and perturbed epithelial integrity were increased compared to placebo. A number of drug-gene interactions were significant (P < .05, false discovery rate).
CONCLUSIONS: Nasal lavage SERPINE1 transcripts increase during viral illness in children with asthma who have the risk allele but not in children without this allele. In asthma exacerbations, the risk allele is associated with augmentation of TGF-β/SMAD3 and epithelial pathways as well as a differential airway transcriptomic response to the type 2 modulator mepolizumab.

nlm_primary_record.title: Efficacy of dupilumab for patients with chronic rhinosinusitis without nasal polyps: A randomized double-blind, placebo-controlled phase II study.
nlm_primary_record.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic rhinosinusitis without nasal polyps (CRSsNP) is a heterogeneous inflammatory disease that affects up to 8% of the population. No biologics are currently approved for CRSsNP, and emerging data suggest that type 2 (T2)-high endotypes may respond preferentially to targeted therapy.
OBJECTIVE: We sought to evaluate the efficacy and safety of dupilumab, an mAb targeting the IL-4/IL-13 signaling pathway, in patients with moderate to severe CRSsNP and to explore differential responses by T2 endotype.
METHODS: In a 6-month, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 33 adults with moderate to severe CRSsNP received dupilumab 300 mg or placebo every 2 weeks. Primary outcomes were change in 22-item Sino-Nasal Outcome Test (SNOT-22) and Mini Rhinoconjunctivitis Quality of Life Questionnaire (MiniRQLQ) scores. Secondary outcomes included computed tomography sinus scores and use of rescue medications. Prespecified subgroup analyses were performed in patients with T2-high CRSsNP, defined by pronounced allergen skin test positivity or elevated blood eosinophils.
RESULTS: Dupilumab significantly improved SNOT-22 (-7.0 vs placebo; P < .001) and MiniRQLQ (-5.2 vs placebo; P < .01) scores. Patients with T2-high CRSsNP showed numerically greater improvement in SNOT-22 (-11.3; P = .07) and significant improvement in MiniRQLQ (-9.2; P < .01) scores. Reductions in computed tomography scores and rescue medication use favored dupilumab but were not statistically significant. Treatment was well tolerated, and all participants completed the study.
CONCLUSION: Dupilumab was associated with meaningful improvements in patient-reported outcomes in adults with CRSsNP. The observed trend toward enhanced benefit in patients with T2-high CRSsNP supports the potential for endotype-directed therapy and underscores the need for larger studies to evaluate the role of T2-targeted biologics in CRSsNP management.

nlm_primary_record.title: Integrated-omics endotyping of patients with chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps and their response to glucocorticoid therapy.
nlm_primary_record.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Integrated-omics approaches provide deeper insights into disease heterogeneity, but combined host immune and nasal microbiota profiles in chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) remain poorly characterized.
OBJECTIVE: We sought to identify biologically distinct CRSwNP endotypes by integrating transcriptomic and microbiota data from nasal brushings and to assess responses to corticosteroid therapy across these endotypes.
METHODS: Baseline transcriptomic and microbiota data from the multicenter COMPASS cohort (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT05598424) were integrated using similarity network fusion and hierarchical clustering. Differential gene expression and bacterial genus abundance analyses were performed to characterize each endotype. In the COMPASS cohort, patients with CRSwNP who had a bilateral nasal polyp score of 4 or more points were enrolled and received 4 weeks of intranasal corticosteroid treatment. Those whose nasal polyp score remained at 4 or more points after intranasal corticosteroid treatment received a 2-week course of add-on systemic corticosteroid therapy. Response rates were compared across endotypes using the chi-square test or the Fisher exact test.
RESULTS: Among 132 patients from 20 hospitals in China, 4 endotypes were identified: 1 non-type 2 inflammatory endotype (cluster A) and 3 type 2 inflammatory endotypes distinguished by microbiota composition-a Corynebacterium-dominated profile (cluster B), a Staphylococcus-dominated profile (cluster C), and a polymicrobial profile (cluster D). Among patients receiving add-on systemic corticosteroid therapy, cluster C showed the highest observed response rate (94.1%), followed by cluster D (72.7%), cluster B (62.5%), and cluster A (56.7%).
CONCLUSIONS: Integrated transcriptome and microbiota analysis identified 4 CRSwNP endotypes with distinct immune-microbial signatures and variable corticosteroid responsiveness, supporting the potential for endotype-driven precision therapy in CRSwNP.

nlm_primary_record.title: Thymic stromal defects and immune dysregulation in hypomorphic recombinase activating gene (RAG) deficiency: Implications for hematopoietic cell transplantation.
nlm_primary_record.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thymic epithelial cells (TECs) are essential for positive and negative selection during T-cell development. Hypomorphic recombinase activating gene (RAG) deficiency is characterized by T-cell lymphopenia and an increased risk of infections and autoimmunity. However, whether abnormalities of TEC composition and function also contribute to these clinical features is unknown.
OBJECTIVE: Using a Rag1 hypomorphic (Rag1mut) mouse model, we examined composition and function of the TEC compartment, both before and after hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
METHODS: Flow cytometry, immunofluorescent imaging, and single-cell RNA sequencing were used to characterize the TECs and thymocytes. Bone marrow transplantation studies were performed to define level of donor chimerism required to fully correct thymic abnormalities.
RESULTS: The thymus of Rag1mut mice is small, with an increased proportion of cortical and a severe reduction of medullary TECs, as well as reduced expression of tissue-restricted antigens. Transplantation of Rag1mut hematopoietic stem cells into wild-type mice phenocopied the altered thymic architecture of Rag1mut mice. Transplantation of wild-type hematopoietic stem cells into Rag1mut mice fully corrected thymocyte development and normalized the TEC phenotype. However, in competitive settings, lower levels of wild-type hematopoietic stem cell engraftment were associated with persistence of mutant-derived double-negative thymocytes and of a low number of Itgβ4-positive, medullary TEC-low cells, incomplete restoration of the TEC compartment, and autoantibody production.
CONCLUSION: Impaired thymocyte development in Rag1mut mice leads to abnormal TEC composition and immune dysregulation, whose correction requires robust levels of donor chimerism after hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.

nlm_primary_record.title: Systemic Allergic Reactions to mRNA COVID-19 Vaccines: A Randomized Placebo-controlled Trial.
nlm_primary_record.abstract:
BACKGROUND: COVID-19 mRNA vaccines were associated in early reports with more allergic reactions than most vaccines, especially in people with allergic histories.
OBJECTIVE: To estimate the proportions of systemic allergic reactions to mRNA COVID-19 vaccines in people reporting prior severe allergic reactions to various allergens, and/or mast cell disorders (PSAR/MCD Group) and determine if proportions are higher than in non-PSAR/non-MCD (Comparison Group).
METHODS: We conducted a multi-center, randomized, double-blinded (for the initial injection), placebo-controlled trial in PSAR/MCD vs Comparison adults and adolescents. Participants received a double-blinded injection with Pfizer-BioNTech or Moderna COVID-19 vaccine or placebo, followed by unblinded vaccine injections. The primary outcome was the incidence of clinically-determined systemic allergic reactions within 90 minutes after injection.
RESULTS: The trial enrolled 723 participants of a planned 3400, with 664 (56% PSAR/MCD) receiving at least one injection. Within 90 minutes of injection, systemic allergic reactions occurred in 5/180 (3%) PSAR/MCD participants given Pfizer-BioNTech (vs 0/133 [0%] Comparison Group; p=0.063) and 2/173 (1%) PSAR/MCD participants given Moderna (vs 0/144 [0%] Comparison Group; p=0.27). Reactions were also reported >90 minutes and ≤48 hours only in PSAR/MCD. Among PSAR/MCD participants, reaction rates to vaccine within 90-minutes and 48-hours were similar to placebo. Extensive laboratory studies did not identify plausible reaction mechanisms.
CONCLUSIONS: Systemic allergic reactions based solely on clinical determination within 90-minutes or 48-hours of vaccination were only observed in PSAR/MCD but failure to achieve planned enrollment limited statistical precision. Reactions to placebo and failure to identify underlying immunologic mechanisms suggest non-allergic or non-immunologic causes.

nlm_primary_record.title: Type I autoimmunity in chronic spontaneous urticaria: Evidence, limits, and endotype overlap.
nlm_primary_record.abstract: Chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) is a mast cell-driven disorder with basophil involvement and several possible upstream mechanisms. Type IIb autoimmune CSU, mediated by functional IgG autoantibodies against FcεRIα or IgE, is the best-validated endotype. Evidence for type I autoimmune (autoallergic) CSU is less complete, but findings involving IgE autoantibodies to thyroid peroxidase (TPO), IL-24, and other self-antigens suggest that IgE-dependent autoreactivity may be relevant in some patients. However, total IgE level, atopy, allergic disease, and timing of the response to omalizumab are not diagnostic of this mechanism. Rather than viewing type I and type IIb CSU as competing categories, we hypothesize 2 potentially overlapping immunologic axes: an IgE-autoantibody axis and an IgG/complement axis. Patients may lie closer to one axis, show markers of both, or remain provisionally idiopathic because current biomarkers cannot classify them with confidence. Progress will require harmonized functional assays; skin, mast cell, and basophil readouts, as well as longitudinal treatment studies. The central question is when an IgE autoantibody is only a passenger, when it is a partner, and when it is the driver of the wheal.

nlm_primary_record.title: Comparative efficacy and safety of antihistamines, increased antihistamine dosing (updosing), and antihistamine adjuncts for chronic urticaria: Systematic review, dose-response, and network meta-analysis of randomized trials.
nlm_primary_record.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic urticaria, an immune-mediated condition characterized by wheals, angioedema, or both lasting for more than 6 weeks, is treated with H1 antihistamines as the first-line therapy. Questions remain regarding the comparative benefits and harms of antihistamines and their adjuncts, and of H1 antihistamine dose escalation.
OBJECTIVE: We analyzed the comparative benefits and harms of antihistamines and their adjuncts (H2 blockers or montelukast) as well as of H1 antihistamine dose escalation.
METHODS: As part of updating the American Academy of Allergy, Asthma & Immunology and American College of Allergy, Asthma & Immunology Joint Task Force on Practice Parameters Chronic Urticaria guidelines, we searched MEDLINE, EMBASE, CENTRAL, and regulatory databases from inception to March 17, 2025, for randomized trials addressing antihistamines or their adjuncts for chronic urticaria. Paired reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias. Random effects network and dose-response meta-analyses addressed urticaria activity, angioedema activity, urticaria-related quality of life, and harms including sedation. The GRADE approach informed certainty of evidence ratings.
PROSPERO: CRD42022367280.
RESULTS: A total of 211 trials (22,187 participants) evaluated 55 unique treatments. Bilastine, desloratadine, and fexofenadine are among the most effective in overall improvement. Cetirizine and loratadine are among the most effective in reducing overall urticaria activity and its subcomponents, with cetirizine also effective in improving urticaria-related quality of life. Second-generation agents may be more effective than first-generation agents in improving urticaria activity and sleep disturbance. Sedation risk likely increases with higher doses, with first-generation agents like diphenhydramine among the most sedating, while sedation risk differs among second-generation agents.
CONCLUSIONS: For chronic urticaria, second-generation agents differ in their efficacy and safety. First-generation agents are less beneficial and more harmful. Escalating to higher daily doses may provide additional benefits but likely increases sedation.

nlm_primary_record.title: Lower nasal sphingolipids in pediatric asthma and cell-type-specific effects of 17q21 variants.
nlm_primary_record.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Genetic variations at the 17q21 asthma-risk locus regulate GSDMB and ORMDL3, influencing inflammatory pathways and sphingolipid metabolism. Although 17q21 variants such as rs7216389 and rs12936231 are associated with ORMDL3 expression in immune and airway smooth muscle cells, their effects on airway epithelial sphingolipids remain unclear.
OBJECTIVES: We sought to determine whether asthma or 17q21 asthma genotypes alter sphingolipid composition in the upper respiratory tract in children and to define contributions of epithelial versus immune cells.
METHODS: Sphingolipids were quantified by mass spectrometry in nasal fluid and plasma from children with and without asthma. Nasal epithelial cells and peripheral blood mononuclear cells from healthy adults homozygous for rs7216389 C/C or T/T (risk) were analyzed for sphingolipid levels and ORMDL3/GSDMB associated gene expression.
RESULTS: Children with atopic asthma had significantly lower nasal dihydroceramides, ceramides, and sphingosine independent of inhaled corticosteroids and allergic rhinitis. Asthma was associated with increased plasma sphingolipids but decreased sphingolipids in blood cells, mirroring nasal findings. In peripheral blood mononuclear cells, the rs7216389 T allele was associated with increased ORMDL3 expression and suppressed de novo sphingolipid synthesis. In nasal epithelial cells, the T allele predominantly increased GSDMB expression and did not alter sphingolipid metabolism.
CONCLUSIONS: Nasal mucosal sphingolipids are reduced in children with atopic asthma, and sphingolipids generated by de novo sphingolipid synthesis may serve as a noninvasive biomarker of disease. 17q21 risk alleles can exert cell-type-specific effects: ORMDL3-mediated suppression of sphingolipid synthesis occurs in immune cells but not in airway epithelial cells. Systemic immune or inflammatory cell-driven alterations may contribute to reduced airway sphingolipids in asthma.

nlm_primary_record.title: Accounting for seasonal variation of nasal gene expression improves transcriptome analysis of asthma.
nlm_primary_record.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Environmental seasonal changes, including allergen exposure, pollutants, and viral prevalence, impact gene expression across human tissues. Therefore, season of sample collection is critical to consider when analyzing disease-associated transcriptional programs.
OBJECTIVE: We sought to investigate the effect of season on identification of asthma-associated genes.
METHODS: We analyzed RNA sequencing data from nasal brushes of patients with asthma (n = 361) and healthy control participants (n = 57) included in the ATLANTIS study. Samples were compared across 2 time periods defined by a data-driven approach: winter-spring (November 15 through May 14) and summer-autumn (May 15 through November 14), correcting for age, sex, smoking, and asthma status. Gene set variation analysis scores of the obtained seasonal gene signatures were compared using Mann-Whitney U test in the independent Prevention and Incidence of Asthma and Mite Allergy cohort (n = 325) for replication.
RESULTS: We identified 1731 genes differentially expressed between the 2 time periods (813 higher expression and 918 lower expression in winter-spring compared with summer-autumn; false discovery rate < .05). This signature was replicated in the Prevention and Incidence of Asthma and Mite Allergy cohort nasal gene expression data and was independent of asthma or allergy status. Samples collected in winter-spring showed a significantly lower predicted proportion of ciliated cells (P = .005) and a higher proportion of basal cells (P = .04) compared with samples from summer-autumn. Crucially, including season as a covariate in models for asthma-associated gene expression nearly doubled the number of differentially expressed genes, from 126 to 271 (false discovery rate < .05).
CONCLUSIONS: Season of sampling strongly affects the nasal transcriptome. We demonstrate that season-adjusted analyses significantly enhance sensitivity for detecting disease-associated changes.

nlm_primary_record.title: Site-specific cutaneous inflammation: Mechanisms and therapeutic implications.
nlm_primary_record.abstract: Inflammatory skin diseases exhibit prominent anatomic distribution patterns that have long guided clinical diagnosis, yet the biological mechanisms underlying site specificity remain incompletely defined. These regional predilections arise from structural, immunologic, and microbial heterogeneity across human skin. Epidermal barrier architecture, which varies substantially between body sites, including 10- to 100-fold differences in stratum corneum thickness as well as prevalence and types of hair follicles and glands, creates distinct microenvironments that shape resident immune populations, microbial communities, and host antimicrobial defenses. The skin harbors an estimated 20 billion tissue-resident memory T cells that persist within anatomically restricted niches, providing a mechanistic basis for disease recurrence at the same sites. In parallel, the skin microbiome contributes to regional specialization by forming distinct communities in oily, moist, and dry regions, which are disrupted in disease-specific ways, while environmental exposures such as ultraviolet radiation, mechanical stress, and humidity further reinforce regional variation. Recent advances in single-cell and spatial transcriptomic technologies have enabled inflammatory responses to be mapped with high precision, allowing detailed interrogation of site-specific cellular interactions and signaling pathways across the skin. Collectively, these findings support a unifying model in which regional tissue properties and local immune ecosystems shape disease-specific inflammatory circuits, accounting for the anatomic predilection of inflammatory diseases and underscoring the importance of tissue context for precision therapeutics.

nlm_primary_record.title: IFN-γ-NOD2/IL-5-FCGR axis enhances eosinophil extracellular trap formation in allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis/mycosis.
nlm_primary_record.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis/mycosis (ABPA/M) is characterized by systemic eosinophilia and eosinophil-rich mucus plugs, but mechanisms programming eosinophil pathogenicity remain unclear.
OBJECTIVE: We aim to define eosinophil activation programs and upstream signals that promote extracellular trap formation in ABPA/M.
METHODS: We performed multi-omics analyses (RNA sequencing and proteomics) of blood eosinophils from healthy participants, patients with eosinophilic asthma, and patients with ABPA/M. Surface-marker profiles were compared between blood and airway eosinophils from patients with ABPA/M. In vitro stimulation assays using IFN-γ, IL-5, and a NOD2 ligand were combined with multi-omics readouts and functional evaluation of IgG cross-linking-induced eosinophil extracellular trap formation.
RESULTS: Multi-omics profiling identified activation patterns consistent with IFN-γ and IL-5 signaling in ABPA/M blood eosinophils. ICAM1 was upregulated on both blood and airway eosinophils, whereas programmed death-ligand 1upregulation was specific to airway eosinophils. Programmed death-ligand 1induction required combined stimulation with IFN-γ and a NOD2 ligand, but not IL-5. Under IFN-γ plus NOD2 ligand stimulation, eosinophils exhibited inflammatory remodeling, including increased Fc gamma receptor expression. Functionally, pretreatment with IFN-γ and a NOD2 ligand enhanced IgG cross-linking-induced extracellular trap formation in an nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate oxidase-dependent manner and required lymphocyte function-associated antigen 1 interactions with ICAM1. Combined stimulation with IFN-γ and IL-5 similarly augmented extracellular trap formation.
CONCLUSION: ABPA/M eosinophils are shaped by mixed inflammatory cues, in which IFN-γ cooperates with fungal-sensing signals or IL-5 to enhance Fc gamma receptor-linked, IgG-triggered extracellular trap formation, potentially contributing to mucus plugging.

nlm_primary_record.title: Comparative efficacy and safety of treatments for eosinophilic esophagitis: Systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
nlm_primary_record.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) is a chronic immune-mediated disease characterized by esophageal dysfunction and eosinophilic inflammation. Comparative efficacy and safety of available therapies remain uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: We sought to compare efficacy and safety of available treatments for EoE in children and adults.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials comparing pharmacologic, dietary, and mechanical interventions. We searched MEDLINE, EMBASE, and CENTRAL to March 17, 2026. Paired reviewers screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias. We conducted random-effects network meta-analysis; assessed certainty using GRADE.
RESULTS: We included 48 randomized controlled trials (3,963 participants). High-frequency dupilumab (mean difference [MD] = -11.08; 95% confidence interval [CI], -15.14 to -7.03; high certainty) and swallowed topical corticosteroids (MD = -6.86; 95% CI, -9.17 to -4.56; moderate certainty) are likely among the most effective for symptoms. Similarly, high-frequency dupilumab (MD = 6.57; 95% CI, 3.42 to 9.71; moderate certainty) and swallowed topical corticosteroids (MD = 7.20; 95% CI, 1.01 to 13.39; moderate certainty) are among the most effective for quality of life. Other interventions, such as certain biologics and epicutaneous immunotherapy, are likely not different from placebo in symptom reduction (moderate certainty). Multiple interventions reduce peak eosinophil counts (high certainty) and likely do not increase harms versus placebo (moderate or high certainty). Four- and 6-food elimination diets may be better than elimination of one in reducing symptoms (low certainty), but no other patient-important, endoscopic, or histologic outcomes, and may involve greater burden.
CONCLUSIONS: High-frequency dupilumab and swallowed topical corticosteroids are among the most effective therapies across patient-important and inflammatory outcomes. Histologic improvements do not guarantee patient-important outcome improvement. Elimination diet comparative benefits are modest and low certainty, and traded off by certain burdens.

nlm_primary_record.title: Refining atopic dermatitis pathogenesis: Early-life trajectories, noncanonical cytokines, and JAK-STAT signaling.
nlm_primary_record.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is increasingly understood as a biologically heterogeneous disease in which barrier dysfunction, type 2 inflammation, neuroimmune dysregulation, and intracellular signaling abnormalities interact in dynamic and context-dependent ways. This review highlights 3 concepts that have advanced the field in recent years. First, studies in early life suggest that AD harbors measurable preclinical abnormalities, developmental trajectories, and potential opportunities for targeted intervention. Second, recent work has refined the cytokine architecture of AD beyond IL-4 and IL-13 by identifying noncanonical cytokine circuits that shape distinct aspects of the disease phenotype, including upstream pathogenic TH2 cell activation, epidermal dysfunction, and itch. Third, rare gain-of-function disorders involving signal transducer and activator of transcription 6 (STAT6) and Janus kinase 1 (JAK1) have consolidated the relevance of the IL-4/IL-13-JAK-STAT signaling axis in AD, providing insight into how specific alterations within this axis can drive severe allergic skin disease and associated systemic phenotypes. Considered together, these developments support a more differentiated view of AD pathophysiology, in which disease onset, tissue inflammation, barrier impairment, pruritus, and therapeutic response are governed by partially overlapping but nonidentical pathways.

nlm_primary_record.title: Precision Diagnosis and Differentiation of Eosinophilic Colitis and Inflammatory Bowel Disease Using a Tissue-Based Molecular Gene Expression Panel.
nlm_primary_record.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Eosinophilic colitis (EoC) and eosinophil-predominant inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) can show overlapping clinical and histologic features, creating diagnostic uncertainty. Whether tissue gene expression can objectively distinguish these conditions in the setting of colonic eosinophilia remains unclear.
OBJECTIVE: We sought to develop and validate a tissue-based molecular diagnostic panel to quantify eosinophilic inflammation and differentiate EoC from IBD-associated colonic eosinophilia.
METHODS: This multi-center study analyzed 88 colonic biopsies from a cohort enriched for children and young adults, including 74 patients with EoC or IBD and non-disease controls. We developed a 96-gene qPCR-based platform, the Colonic Eosinophilia Diagnostic Panel (CEDP), and generated molecular EoC and IBD scores. Diagnostic accuracy was determined by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC).
RESULTS: An EoC score developed from 59 genes (e.g., eosinophil-associated gene CLC) distinguished active EoC from non-disease controls (AUC 0.92, 95% CI 0.78-1.0) and quantified the active molecular eosinophilic inflammatory program, correlating with peak eosinophil counts. However, this score did not differentiate EoC from IBD. An IBD score from 18 genes (e.g., DUOXA2) reflecting inflammatory pathways provided complementary discriminatory information and resolved this overlap. This approach distinguished active IBD from all other groups (AUC 0.98, 95% CI 0.76-1.0) and specifically active EoC (AUC 0.99, 95% CI 0.95-1.0), correlated with endoscopic activity, and differentiated IBD with high colonic eosinophil counts.
CONCLUSIONS: We developed the CEDP with a tissue-based, two-component molecular framework for evaluating colonic eosinophilia. By measuring eosinophilic inflammatory activity and identifying an IBD-associated molecular signature, this platform can distinguish EoC from IBD beyond conventional histopathology alone.

nlm_primary_record.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Inflammation of the olfactory mucosa, rather than airflow obstruction, is a major barrier to olfactory recovery in chronic rhinosinusitis with olfactory dysfunction (CRSwOD). Macrophages, a predominant immune cell population in the olfactory mucosa, play a key role in regulating local inflammation and olfactory neuroregeneration.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the role of Sirtuin 3 (SIRT3) in modulating macrophage function and its impact on olfactory recovery in CRSwOD.
METHODS: Single-cell RNA sequencing, bulk RNA sequencing, and untargeted metabolomics data were analyzed to characterize immune and neuronal alterations in CRSwOD, with a focus on macrophage activation states. In vivo experiments using SIRT3-deficient mice were performed to evaluate olfactory sensory neuron (OSN) integrity, while in vitro assays examined the metabolic and inflammatory profiles of SIRT3-deficient macrophages under inflammatory conditions.
RESULTS: Transcriptomic analysis revealed that olfactory dysfunction was closely associated with the altered functional status of mucosal macrophages. During the progression of chronic rhinosinusitis in mice, loss of SIRT3 exacerbated OSN loss and impaired the protective role of macrophages in maintaining neuronal homeostasis. Mechanistically, SIRT3 deficiency enhanced macrophage proinflammatory activity, increased hypoxia-inducible factor 1α (HIF-1α) expression, promoted glycolysis, and reduced mitochondrial membrane potential.
CONCLUSION: In a mouse model of chronic rhinosinusitis, SIRT3 modulates macrophage-mediated inflammatory metabolism within the olfactory mucosa, thereby protecting against inflammation-induced olfactory damage. These findings provide mechanistic insight into inflammation-driven olfactory dysfunction and identify SIRT3 as a potential therapeutic target for CRSwOD.

nlm_primary_record.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Food allergy (FA) restrictive policies (RPs) are widely used in daycares/schools, but clinicians and families worry policies may increase stigma, bullying, or anxiety; these psychosocial effects have not been characterized.
OBJECTIVE: We sought to examine how FA RPs in daycares/schools impact the psychosocial wellbeing of children with IgE-mediated FA and their parents.
METHODS: We conducted a survey of child-parent pairs recruited from Boston Children's Hospital and through social media. Participants completed self-administered electronic surveys on daycare/school FA policies and validated instruments assessing FA-related psychosocial wellbeing. Inclusion criteria were children aged <18 years with IgE-mediated FA to peanut and/or tree nut who attended daycare/school. Children attending daycares/schools with or without peanut/tree nut RPs and their parents were compared on validated instruments assessing FA-related psychosocial wellbeing.
RESULTS: The cohort included 652 child-parent dyads. Parents were primarily mothers (96.7%). Median child age was 6.0 years. Across all grades, there was no association between presence of RPs and parental FA-related QOL, parent or child FA-related anxiety, or FA-related bullying. In young children, presence of RPs was associated with higher FA-related quality of life (QOL) (daycare/preschool/pre-K p=0.007, elementary p=0.048); no association was found in older children. Presence of any RP was associated with greater parental comfort with FA policies across all grades (p<0.05).
CONCLUSION: We found no evidence that FA RPs impact bullying, FA-related anxiety, or general anxiety among children or their parents. However, FA RPs improved FA-related QOL in younger children. These findings provide novel evidence-based data to inform school FA policy design.

nlm_primary_record.title: Self-reported health history from 70,724 individuals reveals novel HLA associations with allergy and other frequently underreported conditions.
nlm_primary_record.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Variation in the HLA loci, located on human chromosome 6p, has been associated with hundreds of diseases and conditions. However, high levels of polymorphism that characterize the HLA system, coupled with generally modest effect sizes for most phenotypes, necessitate relatively large sample sizes to power association studies; meanwhile, high resolution HLA genotyping remains relatively resource intensive. These constraints limit identification of novel associations. While phenome-wide association studies (PheWAS) in the context of large registries with available electronic health records (EHR) have revealed new insights into the role of HLA in disease, many common health conditions are poorly represented in EHR due to the temporal nature of their occurrence or general underreporting. Further, these studies have generally been conducted with HLA genotyping data imputed from microarrays, rather than direct measurement of high-resolution genotypes.
OBJECTIVE: To overcome these limitations and reveal novel HLA associations we undertook a PheWAS in many previously understudied health conditions.
METHODS: We queried over 290 conditions, diseases and traits from 70,724 subjects registered with NMDP (formerly known as the National Marrow Donor Program) with available high-resolution HLA genotyping (HLA-A, HLA-B, HLA-C, HLA-DRB1, and HLA-DQB1). After stratifying according to self-reported geographic ancestry, we performed a logistic regression analysis adjusting for sex and age for HLA-phenotype association.
RESULTS: We identified 48 significant HLA associations across self-reported geographic ancestry groups, confirming several known associations and uncovered fourteen novel associations. Most novel associations pertained to common infectious or allergic phenotypes that often go under-reported in the EHR. We identified a previously underappreciated yet very strong association between HLA-DRB1*04:01 and self-reported cefaclor adverse-reaction label of unverified mechanism (OR = 3.74, p-value 5.10E-28), which remained highly significant after excluding individuals reporting multiple drug hypersensitivities (OR = 3.13, p-value = 5.60E-15). Exploratory computational co-folding structure-and-affinity prediction identified a potential interaction between cefaclor and the P4 pocket of HLA-DRB1*04:01, providing a hypothesis-generating structural rationale that requires functional validation. If validated in independent cohorts with clinically characterized phenotypes and functional studies, this association may inform pharmacogenomic risk stratification and targeted prevention of adverse drug reactions. Other novel associations found, such as susceptibility to genital warts (HPV) and allergic rhinitis, reveal new insights into the role of specific HLA alleles in immune-mediated disease. Many of these novel associations were replicated in the independent All of Us cohort (AoU), while others showed the same trend for association, confirming the validity of this approach.
CONCLUSION: Collectively, our findings demonstrate the value of integrating population-scale, high-resolution HLA genotypes with phenotyping beyond the EHR to reveal immunogenetic influences on common health outcomes. These findings motivate future functional studies and validation in clinically characterized cohorts to refine mechanistic understanding and determine potential clinical utility.
